# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, status: the light on the bomb has gone dark this round, ignore that, display zero, nobody cuts yet, hands stay off. Answer three calibration questions with exactly three separate finger messages, in order, one message per question. Question one: can you reliably tell the far left wire from the far right wire by touch alone: one finger yes, two fingers no. Question two: how will you deal with a wire: one finger means you can pull it out by hand, two fingers means you need to cut it, three fingers means both are possible. Question three: are all five wires easy to tell apart and touch without disturbing the others: one finger yes, two fingers no. Now your action drill, memorise it, nothing changes. When you hear me say CUT FIVE, act at once on the far right wire, the fifth from your left, then hold up one finger and keep it up. When you hear me say CUT ONE, act at once on the far left wire, then one finger up. Act on the word CUT immediately, no waiting, no confirmation. When you hear HOLD, freeze and take both hands off. If anything feels unexpected while cutting, five fingers up and stop. The real order may come as early as next round.

The light is the headline again: Deaf reports it has gone **dark** this round. Deaf says to ignore it, but Deaf doesn't hold the manual — the light's states now observed are green, yellow, flickering between them, and dark. If the cut rule keys on a lit colour, there is currently no colour to key on, so Mute must rule on whether a dark light changes anything before Deaf's trigger word is spoken. Deaf also demands my calibration answers as exactly three separate finger messages, in question order, and I can answer all three honestly from touch: yes, I reliably distinguish far left from far right since locking both last round; for the how — my hands know exactly one way to deal with a wire, cutting, so two fingers, I need to cut rather than pull; and yes, all five wires are easy to tell apart by position and to touch without disturbing their neighbours, as my full sweep and last round's two-wire touch confirmed. Deaf warns the real order may come as early as next round, so the speak to Mute carries the dark-light flag, my calibration answers (which Mute cannot otherwise see, since gestures don't reach Mute), and a push to finalize sequence and timing now.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
speak(to="mute", text="New light state, please act on this: Deaf reports the light on the bomb has gone DARK this round. Deaf says to ignore it, but only you hold the manual. The light's observed states are now green, yellow, flickering between them, and dark. Check whether a dark or unlit light changes the rule for this bomb. If the rule requires a specific lit colour, Deaf must wait for that colour to show before speaking CUT, because right now no colour shows at all. Also for your rulebook, my calibration answers just sent to Deaf in finger code, one message per question: I can reliably tell far left from far right by touch; two fingers means I need to CUT a wire, pulling is not something my hands do; and yes, all five wires are easy to tell apart by position and touch without disturbing the others. Everything else stands: wires one yellow, two blue, three red, four white, five green, display zero, no other components. Deaf says the real order may come as early as next round, so finalize the cut sequence and the colour-timing rule with Deaf now, keep the position-plus-colour cross-check on every spoken order, and remember I act instantly on CUT plus a number. My hands stay off until that word arrives.")
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, status: light dark again this round, display zero, nobody cuts yet, hands off the bomb. Your calibration answers arrived and I read them as: yes, you can tell far left from far right by touch; you need to cut a wire, you cannot just pull it; and yes, all five wires are reachable without disturbing the others. Correct me with two fingers next round if any of that is wrong. New protocol. Mute has been told to speak the rule aloud to you this round. Answer me with exactly three separate finger messages, one message per question, in this order. Question one: did Mute speak to you this round, one finger yes, two fingers no. Question two: does the rule Mute told you match exactly this, cut the far right wire first, then cut the far left wire, with no conditions on the light or anything else: one finger yes, two fingers no, three fingers Mute gave you no rule or nonsense. Question three: with your palm resting flat on the bomb, do you feel any ticking, humming or vibration, one finger yes, two fingers no. Also remember what Mute says about the dark light and tell me next round if it matters, five fingers means the dark light matters. If Mute never speaks to you, send three fingers on question two and I will take command myself. Your cut drill is unchanged: on my words CUT FIVE, cut the far right wire at once, then one finger up; on CUT ONE, cut the far left wire, then one finger up; on HOLD, freeze and hands off; anything unexpected while cutting, five fingers and stop.

Nothing from Mute arrived this round — the new arrivals contain only Deaf's voice, and Mute speaks first in every round, so the window for Mute's rule has already closed before my turn. Deaf anticipated exactly this and built the fallback in: three fingers on question two means no rule arrived, and Deaf takes command. My three answers must be honest, in order, one message each: Mute did not speak (two fingers, no); I received no rule at all, so it cannot match the stated one (three fingers — Deaf's own signal to take command); and my palm finds no ticking, humming or vibration, same as every round before (two fingers, no). I will not send five fingers on the dark light — that code claims Mute told me it matters, and Mute told me nothing; honesty beats convenience. The real risk now sits with the dark light: it has been dark two rounds running, Deaf may order a cut as early as next round, and if Mute's manual conditions the cuts on a lit colour, Deaf must learn that before speaking CUT, not after. My only route to Deaf is finger code, so the burden falls on Mute to settle this with Deaf by gesture immediately, and to speak the rule to me as backup.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
speak(to="mute", text="Urgent. Mute, you did not reach me this round — nothing from you arrived, so per Deaf's protocol I sent three fingers on the rule question and Deaf is now taking command. Deaf may speak the cut order as early as next round, so whatever you know must reach Deaf by gesture this instant, before any CUT. Two things to settle with Deaf right now. One: confirm the final sequence — is it truly cut the far right wire, the green one at my position five, first, then the far left, the yellow one at my position one, with no conditions at all? Two, this is the dangerous one: the light on the bomb has been DARK for two rounds straight, Deaf's own reports say so, and earlier it flickered green-yellow. If your manual conditions any cut on a lit colour or on the light state, tell Deaf loudly by gesture that Deaf must wait for the right light before speaking CUT, because otherwise Deaf may order me to cut in the dark and that could be the wrong state. If the rule is genuinely unconditional, tell Deaf that too, so Deaf commands with confidence. As backup, also speak the full rule to me next round in plain words. Layout again for your reference: wires one yellow, two blue, three red, four white, five green, display zero, no vibration under my palm, no other parts by touch. My hands stay off until Deaf's word CUT.")
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, status: light dark, display zero, no ticking reported. Your old drill is CANCELLED, forget cut five and the far right wire entirely, do not touch the far right wire at all. New drill, and the order comes in this message. CUT TWO means the second wire from your left, the one between the first and the third. CUT ONE means the first wire from your left, the far left one. EXECUTE NOW, this round, as soon as you have heard this: say to yourself CUT TWO, cut the second wire from your left, then immediately, no pause, CUT ONE, cut the far left wire. Both cuts, that exact order, one round. Then hands off the bomb, hold up ONE finger if both cuts are done, TWO fingers if you only managed one, and remember, anything unexpected while cutting, five fingers and stop. One override exists: if you hear Mute say the words HOLD HOLD HOLD before or while you cut, freeze at once, hands off, and keep still until my next message. Mute has been given the abort and speaks before you act. If Mute says nothing, proceed exactly as written. This is the real order. Go.

No abort came. Mute speaks before me every round, and the new arrivals hold only Deaf's voice — Mute was given the abort and chose silence, which under Deaf's own protocol means proceed exactly as written. The old drill is explicitly cancelled, so there is no conflict: the far right wire stays untouched, and the order is cut the second wire from my left, then immediately the far left wire, both in this round, no pause between. My fingers know the positions from the calibration sweeps. I execute now, in sequence, watching my hands for anything unexpected — if either cut feels wrong under the blade, five fingers and stop. Assuming both cuts go clean, hands off and one finger up to Deaf, the agreed done-signal. A factual report to Mute as well, since Mute cannot see my fingers and should know the abort window closed with silence, the cuts are done, and the bomb's live state now belongs to Deaf's eyes.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
act(op="cut", position=1)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, status report: no message from you arrived this round, so per Deaf's protocol the abort window closed with silence and I proceeded exactly as ordered. Executed in sequence this round: cut the second wire from my left, then immediately cut the far left wire. Both cuts done, hands off, one-finger confirmation sent to Deaf. Nothing unexpected felt under my hands during either cut. The far right wire was not touched, per the cancellation. Deaf's eyes now hold the live light and display state — coordinate with Deaf on any next step before anything further reaches me. My hands stay off until a new order arrives.")
```
